transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-29
- Time: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Attendees: Priya (Redwood AE), Samir & Alex (Redwood SEs), Dana (Mistral CTO), Ethan (Head of ML), Maya (Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
Redwood walked through integration options. Key concerns: SDK language support, connectors for LangChain/LlamaIndex, where to place company gateway (proxy vs direct SDK), rate limiting and quota behavior across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, observability hooks (trace ids, per-request metadata). Customer wants a reproducible benchmark and security packet before proposing Dedicated.

Topics:
- SDKs and quickstarts (Python/Node/Go)
- LangChain / LlamaIndex examples and patterns
- Gateway / proxy topology (sidecar, central API gateway)
- Rate limits, quotas, burst behavior, retries
- Observability hooks: request IDs, tracing, metrics, per-route logs
- Private deployment concerns (VPC peering, KMS, audit logs)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Priya (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm priya from redwood, this is samir and alex on the engineering side. how are you all?
[00:07] Dana (Mistral): doing good, thanks. i pulled in maya and ethan — we wanted to focus on integration specifics today.
[00:12] Priya: great, real quick agenda — SDKs and langchain/llamaindex support, how to wire up via our api or via a customer gateway, and some q&a on quotas and observability. sound ok?
[00:20] Ethan: yep that's perfect. we have a couple of existing POCs using openai and locally-hosted LLMs, so the big questions are latency/cost and also compliance for PII.
[00:30] Alex (Redwood SE): quick question — what's your target latency for production? p50 / p95? and what's your anticipated qps?
[00:36] Ethan: p50 ideally under 80ms for small assistant queries, p95 under 300ms. QPS is bursty right now, avg 25 qps but peaks to 250 during day.
[00:46] Samir (Redwood SE): cool, that helps. for those SLAs Dedicated is usually the sweet spot — reserved capacity gives predictable p95 and you can tune batching & kv cache. hosted can work but the variability is higher.
[00:58] Maya (Infra): on compliance — we need VPC-only control and KMS/HSM for keys. do you support private deployments?
[01:05] Priya: yes, we have Redwood Private — VPC or on-prem option. we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations, audit logs, and SSO via SAML. we'll include SOC2 and ISO artifacts in the security packet.
[01:15] Dana: good. on the integration end — we use langchain heavily and some parts use llamaindex for document stores. do you have examples? how opinionated are your SDKs?
[01:24] Alex: we have official SDKs in python, node and go. for langchain we have example chains and a repo showing prompt templates + streaming. for llamaindex it's more community-driven but we provide a pattern: use our SDK client as the llm wrapper and keep the index local. we'll share a sample repo.
[01:38] Ethan: when you say 'use SDK as wrapper' — is that a direct call to hosted endpoints, or do you recommend routing through our gateway?
[01:45] Samir: depends. two common patterns — direct SDK calls from app servers to Redwood (simple, lowest latency) or route via a customer proxy/gateway if you need central auth, auditing, or rate-limiting. If you put a gateway in front, we recommend preserving request IDs and propagating tracing headers for observability.
[01:59] Maya: our infra team prefers a central gateway because we need consistent auth and to do token exchange. how does Redwood play with gateway timeouts and retries?
[02:07] Alex: Redwood supports chunked/streaming responses and will keep connections open; gateways should be configured with longer timeouts for streaming endpoints. for retries we surface idempotency keys — if you're doing non-idempotent ops we recommend client-side dedup or using request metadata.
[02:20] Dana: rate limits — what's enforced at the account level vs route level? we have multiple services using the same model and want fair share.
[02:27] Priya: we have multi-tier quotas. hosted accounts get per-key rate limits and concurrency thresholds; Dedicated allows per-tenant routing policies and per-route quotas through the console. you can also set soft-limits and burst windows. we'll show the quota config UI in the console demo.
[02:42] Ethan: any built-in throttling to avoid tail-latency spikes when batching kicks in?
[02:46] Samir: yes, the runtime uses continuous batching with adaptive thresholds; for Dedicated you can pin queue sizes and max batch latency. there's a tradeoff: larger batches -> better token cost but potentially higher latency. we expose those knobs.
[02:59] Maya: observability — we need per-request logs, trace ids, token-level cost breakdowns and export to datadog/newrelic.
[03:07] Alex: we emit trace headers and expose per-request metadata (model, tokens, latency) via our logs and metrics. integrations with datadog and prometheus exist, and you can forward logs to S3 or your SIEM. we'll share the schema for the observability hooks.
[03:20] Dana: you mentioned model pinning and rollout — can we do canary and automatic rollback based on evals?
[03:26] Priya: yes, rollouts are first-class. you can create canary splits, tie rollouts to evals/prompts sets and set auto-fallback if quality drops. that should help your ML team safely experiment.
[03:36] Ethan: about LangChain — can we use the Redwood streaming API with langchain's callback handlers?
[03:41] Samir: absolutely, we have stream adapters and an example that plugs into langchain callbacks. there might be minor naming differences but it's straightforward. we'll include a snippet in the repo.
[03:50] Maya: network questions — if we go Private with VPC peering, do you handle egress? what about NAT and IP allowlists?
[03:58] Alex: for Private we can do VPC peering or private link-like setup. egress is customer-managed; we provide static egress IPs for allowlisting if needed. KMS integrations require outbound connectivity for key wrapping unless you host keys in an HSM in your VPC.
[04:15] Dana: we run a mix of short retrieval-style prompts and longer generation for summaries. does quantization cause quality regressions for the summary tasks?
[04:22] Samir: quantization depends on model and workload. Redwood Optimize gives quant suggestion profiles — for retrieval/summaries we tend to recommend mixed precision or GPTQ profiles tuned for your length distribution. part of the PoC we can test quantized variant and measure quality vs cost.
[04:36] Ethan: what's the onboarding time for Dedicated vs Private?
[04:39] Priya: Dedicated — usually 2-4 weeks for provisioning and config. Private with VPC and KMS takes longer, 4-8 weeks depending on network approvals and HSM set up.
[04:50] Dana: budget concerns — do you have example unit economics for a customer doing 10M tokens / month?
[04:56] Priya: yes we'll include a cost model template (tokens, batch sizes, reserved vs on-demand). we'll send a sample spreadsheet tailored to your QPS and prompt lengths.
[05:05] Maya: one more thing: do you have on-prem appliance option? Some regulated customers require fully air-gapped.
[05:10] Alex: yes, on-prem is possible. it is a larger engagement with enterprise licensing. we'll surface the tradeoffs in the packet.
[05:18] (brief cross-talk)
[05:22] Ethan: ok, for the PoC we can give a sample prompt set and a small traffic replay. we'd like you to run a latency/cost profile with both hosted and dedicated configs.
[05:30] Samir: perfect. we'll do a lightweight benchmark first to validate p50/p95, then propose Dedicated sizing for a reservation.
[05:36] Priya: next steps recap — i'll send pricing + security docs; samir will share the langchain/llamaindex snippet and run a bench; maya will give us the gateway config and QPS numbers; and we'll schedule the PoC kickoff.
[05:50] Dana: sounds good. any blockers from your side?
[05:54] Priya: none. we'll follow up with calendar invites. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: conversational pace, occasional filler (ums), some proper nouns transcribed inconsistently (we may show 'llamaindex' as 'lama index' in some downstream exports).
